A storage unit (250) and a secure delivery system (200) employing that storage unit are described. The storage unit (250) has multiple compartments (254, 256), including at least one compartment (256) that is refrigerated. Each refrigerated compartment (256) is paired with both a thermostat and a cooling device. The unit (250) also includes multiple scales (258, 260) corresponding to the compartments, with each compartment having an associated scale. In addition, the storage unit (250) contains a communications module (262) configured to connect with a communications network (205), at least one lid (820) that provides access to the compartments (254, 256), and a lock arranged to hold each lid (820) securely shut.

The storage unit (250) further comprises a control panel (810) that operates the lock. The control panel (810) includes a user interface for accepting information entered by a user, as well as a power source that provides electrical power to both the cooling device and the control panel. The control panel (810) is configured to unlock the lock when the entered information is confirmed as valid by comparison with a code obtained through the communications module (262).
outputs.L3:
The disclosed technology relates to a storage unit and to a secure delivery system that incorporates and uses the storage unit. The storage unit is designed to receive, store, and protect delivered items, including items that may require temperature-controlled storage.

In one implementation, the storage unit includes a plurality of compartments for holding different delivered goods. At least one of the compartments is a refrigerated compartment. The refrigerated compartment includes a thermostat and a cooling device, allowing the temperature within that compartment to be monitored and regulated. This enables the storage unit to maintain perishable or temperature-sensitive items, such as food, groceries, medicine, or other chilled products, under appropriate storage conditions.

Each compartment of the storage unit is associated with a corresponding scale. The scale is configured to measure the contents of the respective compartment, for example by detecting the weight of items placed in or removed from that compartment. The use of individual scales allows the system to determine whether a delivery has been deposited, whether an item has been removed, or whether the contents of a compartment have changed.

The storage unit also includes a communications module, an access lid, a lock, a control panel, and a power source. The communications module allows the storage unit to receive information, such as access codes or delivery instructions, from a remote system, user device, delivery platform, or other authorized source. The access lid provides physical access to the compartments, while the lock selectively secures the lid to prevent unauthorized access. The power source supplies electrical power to components of the storage unit, including the communications module, control panel, lock, scales, thermostat, and cooling device.

The control panel is configured to manage access to the storage unit. In particular, the control panel releases the lock only after validating user input against a code received through the communications module. For example, a delivery person or authorized user may enter an access code at the control panel. The control panel then compares the entered code with a valid code previously received by the communications module. If the entered code is validated, the control panel actuates the lock to release the access lid, permitting access to the compartments. If the entered code is not validated, the lock remains engaged, thereby maintaining the security of the storage unit and its contents.
outputs.L4:
A secure delivery system is provided for receiving, storing, and protecting delivered goods until they are retrieved by an authorized user. The system includes a storage unit connected to a communications network, allowing it to receive delivery information, access codes, status updates, and control instructions from a remote server, delivery service, or user device.

The storage unit is divided into multiple individual compartments, each configured to hold one or more delivered items. Some of the compartments may be refrigerated or temperature-controlled to accommodate perishable goods such as groceries, medications, flowers, or other temperature-sensitive products. These refrigerated compartments may include thermostats for monitoring internal temperature and cooling devices for maintaining the compartment within a desired temperature range. The temperature settings may be adjusted automatically based on delivery information or manually through an authorized control interface.

Each compartment may include a lockable lid or door that prevents unauthorized access. The locks are controlled electronically through a powered control system connected to a central control panel. The control panel may include a keypad, touchscreen, card reader, wireless receiver, biometric reader, or other user-input device. In some embodiments, each compartment may also include an individual scale configured to detect the presence, removal, or weight of a delivered item. The scale data may be used to confirm that a package has been placed into or removed from a compartment, to detect tampering, or to provide delivery verification.

The system further includes a communications module configured to transmit and receive data over a network, such as the Internet, a cellular network, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or another wired or wireless communications system. When a delivery is scheduled, the communications module may receive a unique access code or authentication credential associated with the delivery. This code may be provided to a delivery person, recipient, or other authorized user.

To access a compartment, a user enters identifying information, an access code, or another authentication input at the control panel. The control panel compares the received input with the code or authorization data obtained through the communications module. If the input is validated, the control system unlocks the appropriate compartment while keeping the remaining compartments secured. If the input is not validated, access is denied, and the system may log the failed attempt or transmit an alert.

Once the compartment is unlocked, the user may place an item into the compartment or retrieve an item from it. The system may then relock the compartment automatically after the lid or door is closed or after a predetermined time period. For refrigerated compartments, the cooling device continues to maintain the required temperature while the item remains stored. The thermostat may provide ongoing temperature feedback to ensure that the contents are preserved under suitable conditions.

The secure delivery system therefore enables packages and perishable items to be delivered safely even when the recipient is unavailable. By combining network-based authorization, individually lockable compartments, optional refrigeration, temperature monitoring, scale-based item detection, and powered electronic controls, the system provides secure, verifiable, and temperature-controlled storage for delivered goods.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a secure delivery storage unit with multiple compartments, refrigerated sections, weight scales, network communication, locking lids, and code-based access control.
counterfactuals.output: A secure delivery storage unit includes a housing defining a plurality of separately accessible storage compartments, at least one of the compartments comprising a refrigerated section configured to maintain a selected temperature range for temperature-sensitive deliveries. Each compartment includes a lockable lid or door controlled by an electronic locking mechanism. One or more weight sensors are associated with respective compartments to detect placement, removal, or weight changes of delivered items. A control module is operatively coupled to the locking mechanisms, weight sensors, refrigeration system, and a network communication interface. The control module is configured to receive delivery information over a network, generate or validate access codes, selectively unlock designated compartments in response to authorized code entry, monitor compartment status, and transmit delivery, access, temperature, lock, and weight data to a remote server or user device. The storage unit thereby provides controlled, verifiable, and monitored receipt and retrieval of deliveries, including refrigerated goods, without requiring recipient presence.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a "Disclosed herein..." patent summary describing a smart parcel/grocery delivery box numbered as storage unit 250 in secure delivery system 200, including compartments 254/256, scales 258/260, communications module 262, lid 820, and control panel 810.
counterfactuals.output:
Disclosed herein is a secure delivery system 200 including a smart storage unit 250 configured to receive, secure, monitor, and facilitate retrieval of parcels, groceries, prepared foods, or other delivered items. In some embodiments, the storage unit 250 includes a housing defining one or more internal storage compartments, including a first compartment 254 and a second compartment 256. The compartments 254, 256 may be independently accessible, independently lockable, thermally insulated, temperature controlled, or otherwise adapted for different types of deliveries, such as dry goods, refrigerated groceries, frozen goods, prescriptions, or high-value parcels.

In certain embodiments, the storage unit 250 includes one or more sensing devices configured to detect placement, removal, weight, condition, or presence of delivered items. For example, a first scale 258 may be positioned in or associated with the first compartment 254, and a second scale 260 may be positioned in or associated with the second compartment 256. The scales 258, 260 may generate weight data before, during, or after a delivery event to verify that an item has been deposited, to determine whether a delivered item corresponds to expected order information, to detect tampering or unauthorized removal, or to update an inventory record associated with the storage unit 250.

The storage unit 250 may further include a communications module 262 configured to communicate with one or more remote devices, servers, delivery-provider systems, user devices, merchant systems, or access-control services. The communications module 262 may support one or more wired or wireless communication protocols, including Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth, near-field communication, Ethernet, Thread, Zigbee, or other suitable communication technologies. In some embodiments, the communications module 262 receives delivery authorization data, transmits delivery status notifications, reports sensor data from the scales 258, 260, receives access credentials for delivery personnel, and communicates lock, temperature, power, or tamper-status information.

In some embodiments, the storage unit 250 includes a lid 820 movable between open and closed positions to permit access to at least one of the compartments 254, 256. The lid 820 may include or cooperate with an electronically controllable locking mechanism configured to secure the compartments after a delivery has been deposited. The lid 820 may be hinged, sliding, segmented, or otherwise configured to selectively expose one or more compartments. In some implementations, the lid 820 is automatically unlocked in response to validation of a delivery code, a mobile-device credential, biometric data, a one-time passcode, a remote authorization command, or other access permission received or verified by the secure delivery system 200.

The storage unit 250 may also include a control panel 810 disposed on or coupled to the housing. The control panel 810 may include a display, keypad, touchscreen, indicator lights, audio interface, camera, scanner, microphone, speaker, biometric reader, or other user-interface elements. The control panel 810 may be configured to receive access credentials from a delivery agent or user, display compartment status, provide delivery instructions, present pickup confirmations, initiate compartment unlocking, or guide a delivery workflow. In some embodiments, the control panel 810 communicates with the communications module 262 and one or more controllers of the storage unit 250 to coordinate authentication, locking, weighing, notification, and logging operations.

In operation, the secure delivery system 200 may receive delivery information corresponding to an expected delivery, including an item identifier, expected weight, temperature requirement, delivery window, authorized carrier, access credential, or compartment assignment. Upon arrival, a delivery agent may interact with the control panel 810 or a mobile device to request access to the storage unit 250. The system 200 may authenticate the delivery agent and unlock the lid 820 or a selected compartment 254, 256. After the item is placed in the assigned compartment, the corresponding scale 258 or 260 may measure the weight of the delivered item. The measured weight may be compared with expected delivery data, stored in a delivery record, and transmitted via the communications module 262 to a user device, merchant system, or delivery management platform. The lid 820 may then be locked, and a notification may be sent indicating that the delivery has been secured.

In some embodiments, the storage unit 250 may detect removal of an item by monitoring a change in weight measured by the scales 258, 260, sensing opening of the lid 820, or receiving a user authentication at the control panel 810. The system 200 may generate an audit trail including times of access, identities or credentials used for access, compartment identifiers, measured weights, sensor events, images, temperature data, and communication records. The storage unit 250 may thereby reduce failed deliveries, prevent theft or spoilage, verify delivery completion, and support secure unattended receipt of parcels or groceries.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention disclosure paragraph for a connected refrigerated delivery locker that can weigh contents and unlock only after a user enters a valid code received over a communications network.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a connected refrigerated delivery locker configured to securely receive, store, verify, and release temperature-sensitive goods. In one embodiment, the locker includes an insulated enclosure, a refrigeration unit controlled by a temperature controller, an electronically actuated lock, a weight sensor positioned to measure the contents of the locker, and a network communication module configured to communicate with a remote server, delivery platform, or user device. Upon placement of goods into the locker, the system may detect and record the weight of the contents, associate the measured weight with an order or delivery identifier, and transmit delivery status, temperature data, and weight data over a communications network. A recipient may receive an access code via the network, such as by text message, email, application notification, or server-generated message. The locker remains locked until a user enters a valid access code through a keypad, touchscreen, wireless interface, or other input device, whereupon a controller verifies the code locally or through the remote server and actuates the lock to permit access. The system may further compare measured weight before and after access to confirm pickup, detect tampering, identify partial removal of contents, or update inventory status, thereby providing secure, refrigerated, network-connected delivery and retrieval of perishable items.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: In formal patent language, describe a secure storage unit for home deliveries with plural compartments, at least one cooled compartment, scales for each compartment, network connectivity, lockable access lids, and a control panel that validates user input against a received access code.
counterfactuals.output:
A secure storage unit for receipt of home deliveries is provided. The secure storage unit comprises a housing defining a plurality of discrete storage compartments, each storage compartment being configured to receive one or more delivered articles. At least one of the plurality of storage compartments comprises a temperature-controlled compartment including a cooling system configured to maintain an interior region of the temperature-controlled compartment below an ambient temperature.

Each of the plurality of storage compartments is associated with a respective weighing device arranged to determine a weight of contents received within the corresponding storage compartment. Each storage compartment further includes a lockable access lid movable between a closed position, in which access to the corresponding storage compartment is restricted, and an open position, in which access to the corresponding storage compartment is permitted. Each lockable access lid is operatively coupled to an electronically controllable locking mechanism.

The secure storage unit further comprises a communication interface configured to communicate over a network with at least one remote computing system, and to receive, from the at least one remote computing system, an access code associated with a delivery or user. A control panel is provided on or in communication with the housing, the control panel including a user input interface configured to receive user-entered access information.

A controller is operatively coupled to the communication interface, the control panel, the weighing devices, the cooling system, and the electronically controllable locking mechanisms. The controller is configured to compare the user-entered access information received at the control panel with the access code received via the communication interface and, upon determining that the user-entered access information corresponds to the received access code, selectively actuate at least one of the electronically controllable locking mechanisms to unlock at least one corresponding lockable access lid. The controller may further be configured to record weight data from the respective weighing devices, monitor occupancy or removal of articles from the plurality of storage compartments, and transmit status information over the network.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
